S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.

subtypes.Childlike Silliness: Inappropriate, childish, or illogical behavior appearing in situations.
subtypes.Stupor: No psychomotor activity; not actively relating to environment.
subtypes.Catalepsy: Passive induction of a posture held against gravity.
subtypes.Waxy Flexibility: Slight, even resistance to positioning by examiner.
subtypes.Mutism: No, or very little, verbal response despite the ability to speak.
subtypes.Negativism: Opposition or no response to instructions or external stimuli without apparent motive.
subtypes.Posturing: Spontaneous and active maintenance of a posture against gravity.
subtypes.Mannerism: Odd, circumstantial caricature of normal actions.
subtypes.Agitation: Excessive motor activity without obvious external cause.
subtypes.Grimacing: Contorted facial expressions irrelevant to the situation.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.

subtypes.Diminished Emotional Expression: A state of reduced emotional expression in facial expressions, eye contact, intonation of speech, and movements.
subtypes.Avolition: A decrease in motivated self-initiated purposeful activities.
subtypes.Alogia: A state where the quantity of spontaneous speech is significantly reduced.
subtypes.Anhedonia: A decrease in the ability to experience pleasure or interest in enjoyable activities.
subtypes.Asociality: A state where interest in social activities or interpersonal relationships is significantly reduced.

symptom.disease_info: Schizophrenia is a chronic psychotic disorder defined by persistent disturbances such as delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech or behavior, and negative symptoms, with clear social or occupational decline and a course lasting at least six months. It is distinguished from brief psychotic disorder, delusional disorder, mood disorders with psychotic features, and substance- or medical-condition-related psychosis by its duration, breadth of symptoms, functional impairment, and absence of a primary mood or toxic cause.

patient.stressor_event: Gaining a new family member (e.g., birth, adoption, older adult moving in)
patient.stressor: Leona and her spouse took in an older relative after a housing disruption, turning their Brooklyn apartment into a caregiving space and sharply reducing Leona’s time for yoga, galleries, journaling, and quiet case preparation. Over 8 months, the strain coincided with the emergence of fixed beliefs that intruded into her work and neighborhood life, occasional behavior in sessions and meetings that colleagues found markedly out of context, and a noticeable drop in her usual warmth, initiative, and social engagement. Although she continued working, grant deadlines slipped, clients were reassigned from her heaviest caseload, and her husband observed that she no longer sought out the cultural and community activities that had anchored her. Because of her clinical background and a supervisor’s discreet concern, she requested a confidential psychiatric consultation through a professional referral network.

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: I know it sounds unlikely, but I’ve become convinced that certain comments in staff emails and even the way people pause outside my office are meant to signal that I’m being watched or evaluated, and reassurance from my supervisor hasn’t really shaken that feeling.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.
S022.manifestation: A few times in team meetings or even with clients, I’ve caught myself arranging pens in these exact patterns or repeating a phrase someone just said before I can stop myself, and people look at me like I’ve stepped outside the room somehow.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.
S023.manifestation: What finally brought me in is that I feel like the part of me that used to reach for people and take pleasure in my work, yoga, galleries, even journaling, has gone very quiet, and I’m mostly just moving through obligations.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’m still showing up to work, but I’ve missed grant deadlines and my supervisor has quietly moved some of my more demanding clients to other clinicians because I’m not functioning at my usual level.
add_requirements.duration: This whole change in how I’m thinking, working, and connecting with people has been going on for about eight months, since we took my older relative into our apartment.
add_requirements.psychotic_symptoms_duration: The more clearly unsettling parts, like feeling that emails and hallway pauses are directed at me, have been present for about the past two months.
